Comments and backlinks in documents

Select text in a document and comment on it — the comment attaches to that range and shows as a dot in the right margin. Type @ to mention a cluster, document, card or person, and backlinks show everywhere the document is referenced from.

Updated November 17, 2026

Documents carry annotation in the margins, so the text stays clean and the apparatus stays visible.

Comments on a range

Select text and add a comment, from the toolbar or with ⌘⌥M. A box opens beside the words; Enter posts it. The comment anchors to that range, not to a character position, so editing around it keeps it attached to the right passage.

Commented text is tinted, with a dot in the right margin; a darker dot means there is something in the thread you haven't read. Click the words, or the dot, and the side panel opens on their thread, with the words turned gold while it is open.

Every comment in one place

Comments in the document's header opens the side panel on its comments: every open thread in the document as a short row, in the order they come in the text, with the words it is on, who started it and how much was said since. Press a row and it opens into the whole conversation, with the box to reply in; its quote takes you to its words, opening the page they are on.

In the open thread you can:

  • Reply — Enter sends, Shift+Enter starts a new line. Words you typed and didn't send are kept for you in this browser.
  • Resolve it. It moves to Resolved at the bottom of the panel, which opens on a press, and says who resolved it. Reopen brings it back, and so does a reply. A resolved thread's words read as plain text again; picking it in the panel still lights them.
  • Edit a comment you wrote, from its ⋯ menu. It is marked edited.
  • Copy link to a comment: the link opens the document's cluster, the document and this thread.
  • Delete a comment or the whole thread.

Resolving and deleting show a toast with Undo. Esc puts you back in the text.

Comments thread, resolve, and support @ mentions that notify the person you name. See Comments for the full model, which is shared with the canvas and with notes, and Notifications for who is told about a new comment, a reply or a resolve.

Because a text comment is part of the document, it follows edit access. A viewer sees the dots and reads every thread, by clicking the words or in the side panel; adding, replying to, resolving or deleting a comment needs edit access. Among people who can edit, only the person who wrote a comment can change its words.

Links and mentions

Type @ to reference a cluster, document, card or person. Mentions render as links with hover previews and register as backlinks on the target.

URLs typed or pasted become links automatically.

See Links and mentions.

Backlinks

The Referenced by panel lists everywhere this document is linked or mentioned from — other documents, notes, cards, messages.

Backlinks are the reason mentioning things is worth the keystroke: a location's cluster ends up listing the script scene, the reference board and the message thread that all pointed at it, without anybody maintaining an index.

Bookmarks

Not annotation but adjacent: bookmarks are durable anchors into specific places in a document, listed under the page tree. They survive edits around them, so a bookmark on "the end of act two" stays there as the act changes length.

Frequently asked questions

What happens to a comment if I edit the text it is attached to?

It follows the text. Comments anchor to the range, not to a character offset, so editing around them keeps them attached to the right passage.

What are the dots in the margin?

Comments. Each commented passage has a dot in the right margin. Click one to open its thread.
